title: Indian economic development
examples: What were the main goals of the planning commission?
How did the reforms of 1991 change Indian business?
Can you explain the difference between the primary and secondary sectors?

explain.say: First we will say about the planning period in India.

draw.text: Planning in India: Goals and structure

explain.say: The planning commission set goals for economic growth.
Next we look at the big changes in 1991.
The reforms opened the economy to global trade and investment.
Finally we examine the three economic sectors in India.
In real life, when you buy a phone, you see all three sectors working.

faq.q: What was the main idea behind the planning commission?
faq.a: The planning commission aimed to guide the country's economic development through systematic plans. It helped allocate resources across different sectors for growth.
asks: What was the role of planning in India?
How did India plan its economy?

faq.q: What did the 1991 reforms actually do to the economy?
faq.a: The reforms moved India away from strict government control towards a more market-driven system. This allowed private businesses to operate more freely.
asks: Were the 1991 reforms a big change?
What was the impact of the 1991 liberalization?

faq.q: How do the three sectors relate to each other?
faq.a: The sectors are interconnected; primary activities provide raw materials for the secondary sector. The tertiary sector then uses these goods.
asks: Can you give an example of the three sectors together?
What is the relationship between primary and tertiary sectors?

faq.q: Did the planning commission control everything in India?
faq.a: No, it suggested guidelines, but the market and private enterprise also played a role. The reforms later reduced this central control.
asks: Was the government too controlling before 1991?
What was the government's role before the reforms?

faq.q: Is the service sector the biggest sector now?
faq.a: Yes, the tertiary or service sector has grown to become the largest contributor to India's GDP. This includes IT and finance.
asks: Which sector is most important today?
What is the current dominant sector in India?

facts: The planning commission formulated Five-Year Plans to guide development.
The 1991 reforms initiated a shift towards a market-oriented economy.
The primary sector involves extracting raw materials like agriculture.
The tertiary sector includes services such as banking and IT.

quiz.say: Before 1991, the Indian economy was mainly guided by:
quiz.why: Central planning meant the government heavily directed economic activities.

wrong.0: Market forces rely on supply and demand, which were restricted before 1991.
wrong.1: While aid was received, the primary guide was internal planning policy.
wrong.2: Private investment was present but heavily regulated by the state.

quiz.say: Which sector is responsible for manufacturing goods like cars?
quiz.why: The secondary sector takes raw materials and converts them into finished goods.

wrong.0: Planning is a policy tool, not an economic sector itself.
wrong.2: The primary sector only deals with raw materials, not making things.
wrong.3: The tertiary sector deals with services, not physical production.

quiz.say: The shift towards global trade after 1991 is best described as:
quiz.why: Liberalisation means removing restrictions to allow free interaction with global markets.

wrong.0: Nationalisation means the state takes control, the opposite of what happened.
wrong.1: Protectionism involves high barriers to keep foreign goods out.
wrong.2: Isolationism means cutting off all international economic ties.
